# Distribution policy

A finished piece has a home channel and a distribution order, decided when the piece
is finished rather than negotiated per channel afterward.

The company site is the canonical home of every long-form piece. Canonical means the
full evidence lives there: other channels carry adaptations that link back, and a
correction made to the canonical version is propagated to every adaptation the same
day.

Adaptations may shorten, never sharpen. A channel version may cut context and depth
for the channel's reading pattern, but it may not strengthen a claim, drop a hedge,
or quote a number without its denominator to fit a character limit. When a claim
cannot survive the channel's constraints intact, the adaptation carries the finding's
one-sentence version and the link, nothing more.

Syndication to third-party publications follows the same rule with one addition: the
third party's edits are reviewed against the evidence standards before publication,
and a publication that insists on sharpening a claim gets the piece withdrawn, not
negotiated.

Republication cadence is bounded: a piece may be re-distributed when its finding is
still true and its evidence still current, verified by an actual re-read, not by the
calendar. Re-running a piece whose numbers have drifted is publishing a known error.

## Embargoes

A piece under embargo carries its release condition in the draft header from the
first word, and every reviewer sees it. Distribution before the condition clears is
a process failure regardless of intent, and clearing conditions is a named human's
decision, never inferred from a date alone.
